note: Build a value-focused three-column skeleton, targeting the C5 blend overhead and clean C6 versus C7+ cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Start with a three-column value skeleton: separate C2-C5 overhead, C6-C9 bottoms; recover C5 blend and C6/heavy cuts. Inspect duties/purity/cost, then add only profitable finishing columns and tune expensive splits.
Initial feed split is N-pentane/2,2-DMB (13 K gap). T split is N-butane/isopentane (28 K gap), expected to make a C5 blend bottoms. B split is cyclohexane/heptane (18 K gap), leaving C6 cuts overhead and C7-C9 bottoms. Use moderate 50-60 stages and R/B 2.5-3 to gauge costs.

note: Reconfigure all three columns to clean C4 and C5 blend cuts, with sharper separation and much lower operating pressure.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable blend baseline: root C4/C5 split, T removes C2-C3 from C4 blend, B removes C5 blend from C6+. Then tune purity/cost and add finishing columns only where value exceeds cost.
The first cuts were far too diffuse and produced no sales. Root was nominally nC5/DMB, but C4/C5 is the more useful first split. T should yield C4 mix bottoms; B should yield C5 mix overhead. Increase stages and reflux substantially, and reduce column pressure to 9.6 bar (dp=.6) to improve volatility and test the large potential energy/capital saving. Target C4+C5 blend revenue around $750M/yr before heavy-product upgrades.

note: Move to low pressure, sharpen the C5 and C6 blend cuts, and add a light-ends rejection column so the C4 blend can also sell.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish sales from C4, C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then improve the most valuable cuts and reduce cost. Step 1: rerun the three-cut skeleton at low pressure with sharper T/B separations and add a C2-C3/C4 splitter.
Low pressure is essential: comparable columns at dp=.6 cost several times those at dp=.1, mainly because cold condensers are expensive. The existing root makes a useful C5/C6 boundary. T must send C5 to bottoms; its overhead still needs TT to reject ethane/C3 before the C4 blend can sell. B overhead is already 92% C6 paraffin, so more reflux/stages should reach 95%. Potential blend revenue is about $0.19B C4, $0.60B C5 and $1.05B C6 annually.

note: Rebuild around the two most valuable blends: root C4-/C5, then C5/C6, followed by a much sharper C6-paraffin versus heavier cut.
notebook:
PLAN: First establish the two high-value C5 and C6-paraffin blend sales with a C4-/C5 root, C5/C6 second column, and C6-paraffin/heavy third column. Then add light or heavy product columns only where incremental revenue clearly exceeds cost.
The prior root cut within C5 stranded much of the C5 blend in the heavy branch. Reducing root boil-up from 4 toward 2.5 should move the cut to C4-/C5. In B, reducing boil-up from 6 to 3.5 should make a clean C5 overhead instead of a mixed C5/C6 overhead. R138 confirms that a heavy-branch C6 cut is feasible, but its 100-stage C6 paraffin/naphthene split at reflux 6 was far too sloppy; use 120 stages and reflux/boil-up 8. Light ends are initially discarded to avoid paying for their separation before the main blends sell.

note: Rebuild from a converged root, move the light-column cut to C4/C5, and sharpen the C6-paraffin/heavy separation.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a converged three-column plant selling C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then add a C3/C4 column and finally a C6-naphthene/heavy column if their margins justify cost. I am rebuilding from R185's converged root and resetting its two child cuts.
R185 root 50/4/6 gives a good C5-/C6 split. Its T=60/8/4 cut within n-butane, so raising T boil-up to 8 should place all C4 overhead and yield a clean C5 bottoms blend. Its B=70/6/5 nearly isolated C6 paraffins but leaked C5 and naphthenes; use 120 stages, reflux 8 and boil-up 4.5 to sharpen that cut. Remove BT because it mistakenly split within C6 paraffins. Next add TT to split C3 from C4, making both light blends saleable.

note: Push the remaining butane out of the C5 blend, sharpen the C6-paraffin cut, and reduce the expensive root duty.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a converged low-cost core selling C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then add light-product or naphthene recovery only if margins justify it. Step 1: make both core blends saleable while cutting root cost.
Current root 50/4/6 gives a useful C5-/C6 split but costs $306.5M. T 60/8/8 leaves 20% n-butane in TB; much more boil-up should push C4 overhead and make C5 saleable. B 120/8/4.5 gives 89% C6 paraffins; use 80/10/4.5 for a cheaper, somewhat sharper rectification. Root is reduced to 40/3/4 to lower its dominant cost. Ignore heavy bottoms and light tops for now. R232 shows high-reflux small columns can be cheap, but its root cut sacrifices most feed value.

note: Use cheaper low-pressure columns and strong boil-up to make the C4, C5, and C6-paraffin blend products saleable.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a low-pressure four-column core selling C4, C5 and C6-paraffin blends; first make all three cuts saleable, then reduce duties/stages and only add other recovery if clearly profitable.
Prior 40/3/4 root plus 60/8/16 light split left C5 at 89% (9% C4), while 80/10/4.5 heavy split left C6 badly contaminated by C5. Much higher reboil ratios are needed to expel the light key from each bottoms product. R275 demonstrates that 35-45 stage columns at dp=0.3 cost far less than my tall dp=0.1 columns. Now test root 40/4/5, T 50/6/20, B 50/6/18 and a C3/C4 splitter TT 35/4/8. Target saleable C5 bottoms, C6-paraffin tops and C4 bottoms; discard unsold heavy/light ends.

note: Adopt the profitable blend core, use the demonstrated cheaper C3/C4 splitter, and remove the column whose outlets are both unsold.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from the proven profitable C5/C4 core, remove unsold branches, then reduce root and light-column costs while protecting both blend specifications; only revisit heavy recovery if the core is firmly positive.
R324 earns $736.5M from C5 and C4 blends. Its ethane-rejection column sells nothing and should be removed. R326 shows that TT at 50/5/5 still gives a fully qualifying C4 blend for $61M versus $78M at 60/8/6, though recovery is slightly lower. Copy R324, apply that cheaper TT, and sell TTT. Next test lower root stages/duty and T settings; dp=0.1 separates much better than dp=0.3.

note: Trim only the expensive C4/C5 splitter, retaining strong boil-up and most of its reflux so both blend specifications should survive.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven C5/C4 blend core in small isolated steps: first reduce the expensive T column while preserving both blend specifications, then trim root duty/stages; only add recovery branches if their revenue clearly exceeds cost.
Current best is 0.329 with root 50/4/6, T 60/8/12, TT 50/5/5, all dp=0.1. Root and T cost $306.5M and $211.6M versus TT $61M. C5 blend has only ~4% impurities, so root/T changes are risky. R371 shows simultaneous reductions destroy both products. Now test T 50/7/12 alone. Heavy C6 recovery is unattractive: R373 added $558M cost for $330M extra revenue.

note: Adopt the demonstrated higher-reward baseline before making any further optimization changes.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R418 as the new baseline, then reduce root and T duties cautiously one at a time; retain the demonstrated TT 50/5/4 C4 cut. Add no heavy recovery unless a much cheaper scheme emerges.
R418 earns $737M with costs $570.7M for reward 0.379. Its TT boil-up reduction from 5 to 4 both cuts cost and improves C4 revenue. My reduced T column lost C4 purity, so keep T at 60/8/12. Root remains the largest cost ($306.5M).

note: Adopt R470's better C4/C5 splitter and reduce the root from 50 to 40 stages at unchanged operating conditions, targeting its dominant capital cost without intentionally moving the cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Use R470's slightly better T=60/7/12 core, then optimize the dominant root cost by reducing stages while holding its successful cut and duties. Next tune root reflux/boil-up only if product revenue survives; retain TT=50/5/4 and avoid heavy recovery.
R418 baseline: reward .379, revenue $737.0M, cost $570.7M. R470 improves to .382 by lowering T reflux to 7 (cost -$13.7M, revenue -$9.6M). TT boil-up 4 is better than 5. Reduced TT stages hurt C4 recovery. Root is $306.5M, over half total cost; test 40 stages at unchanged 4/6/.1 to seek capital savings without changing the C5/C6 cut materially.

note: Adopt R518's best core and moderately lower root operating pressure, targeting its dominant energy and temperature cost without changing the separation targets.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R518's best 0.383 core, then reduce the dominant root energy/temperature cost by a moderate pressure drop. If revenue survives, scan pressure further; otherwise test a small root reflux reduction. Retain T=50/7/12 and TT=50/5/4; avoid heavy recovery.
R518: 50/4/6/.1 root, 50/7/12 T, 50/5/4 TT gives reward .383, revenue $727.4M, cost $559.3M. Root costs $306.5M and stage reductions do not reduce its cost, so energy/pressure is the useful lever. T boil-up 10 destroys C5 sales; do not reduce it. Current test raises root pressure drop from .1 to .2, seeking lower temperature/duty cost while preserving the C5/C6 split.

note: Restore the proven 0.383 core and test a modest increase in root reflux to reduce boil-up-driven energy demand later only if the split remains stable; first establish the reflux-cost/purity tradeoff.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R518's 0.383 core and optimize the dominant root energy cost with small, safe operating changes. Test root reflux 4.5 first; if C5 purity/revenue survives, scan toward 4.0, otherwise retain 4.0. Keep T=50/7/12 and TT=50/5/4 unchanged.
R518 settings 50/4/6/.1 root, 50/7/12 T, 50/5/4 TT: reward .383, revenue $727.4M, cost $559.3M. Root dp .2 was disastrous: C5 product lost and total cost rose. Root reflux 3.5 failed to converge, so only modest reflux changes are sensible. T boil-up 10 destroys C5 sales; do not reduce it. Stage reductions do not materially lower root cost.

note: Restore the best core and add a modest ethane-rejection column so the currently wasted C3-rich overhead can sell as C3 mix.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R518's 0.383 core and add a small ethane/C3+ column at TTT. If C3 mix sells profitably, tune this column; otherwise revert to R518 and test root/T cost trims.
R518: root 50/4/6/.1, T 50/7/12/.1, TT 50/5/4/.1; revenue $727.4M, cost $559.3M. Root reflux 4.5 loses $34M revenue and saves only $10.6M cost. Root dp .2 and boil-up 5.7 lose revenue. T boil-up 10 destroys C5 sales; root reflux 3.5 fails.
TTT has ~286 mol/s C3, 34 ethane, 32 isobutane. Removing ethane overhead and isobutane overhead/bottom should make C3 mix worth about $73-75M/yr. Test 40 stages, reflux 3, boil-up 4 at dp .1; small feed should limit cost, though cold condenser may be expensive.

note: Adopt R709's profitable core and lower only the ethane stripper boil-up, seeking greater C3 recovery in its saleable bottoms with less energy.
notebook:
PLAN: Copy the demonstrated R709 0.475 core, then optimize only its cheap ethane-rejection column to recover more saleable C3 mix at lower duty; retain the best valid result and use remaining solves for conservative improvements.
R709's TT 65 stages/reflux 7 sharply improves C4 recovery and makes TTTB saleable, giving .475. Its TTT bottoms contain only 155 of about 273 mol/s feed C3, while 40 stages/reflux 3 already remove ethane effectively. Lowering TTT boil-up from 4 to 2 should leave more C3 in the bottoms and reduce reboiler cost, provided ethane still goes overhead. Root boil-up 5.9 and T 40-45 stages are proven minor savings, but R709's sharper TT split is the main gain.

note: Lower only the ethane stripper boil-up further to recover additional saleable C3 while keeping ethane overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the 0.502 four-column core. First reduce only the cheap ethane stripper boil-up to recover more C3; then use remaining full-plant evaluations to cautiously lower root duty while retaining C5-blend purity.
Current TTT at boil-up 2 gives 206 mol/s saleable C3 versus 155 at boil-up 4 and costs only $8.1M/yr. Ethane remains entirely overhead, so boil-up 1.5 should move more C3 into the bottoms without losing ethane removal. Root and T dominate costs ($304M and $195M/yr); after this one-column test, root boil-up 5.9 is the best target because TB has only 1% DMB and therefore some C6-leakage margin. Avoid pressure changes, which previously performed poorly.

note: Adopt the proven 0.524 stripper setting and modestly reduce root boil-up to target its dominant energy cost while monitoring C5 blend purity.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the best four-column blend core and use remaining solves to reduce dominant root/T energy costs while retaining C4/C5 blend purity. Step 1: adopt the demonstrated 0.524 core (stripper boil-up 1.0); Step 2: cautiously reduce root boil-up, then T only if product margins remain safe.
R807 confirms stripper boil-up 1.0 raises reward to 0.524 and C3 revenue to $62.4M/yr. Root and T still cost $304M and $195M/yr, overwhelmingly energy-related: stage cuts barely helped. TB has only 1% DMB, giving limited but real margin for less root boil-up. Test root 5.5 versus 5.9; stop if C5 blend fails. Avoid pressure changes and new heavy-end columns, which performed poorly or are too costly.

note: Adopt the best 0.539 core and extend the demonstrated ethane-stripper trend to minimum boil-up, seeking additional saleable C3 recovery at negligible cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R854's validated 0.539 core and spend remaining solves extending the clearly profitable ethane-stripper recovery trend; retain every other setting unchanged.
R854/R855 show stripper boil-up 0.5 gives reward 0.539, C3 revenue $65.9M/yr, and only $5.2M/yr column cost. Lowering boil-up from 1.5 to 1.0 to 0.5 monotonically increased saleable C3 recovery. Test the minimum 0.1 now. Root boil-up 5.5 was harmful (reward fell to 0.443), and stage cuts save almost nothing, so leave the core untouched. If 0.1 fails or over-strips the C3 stream, revert to R854.

note: Restore the validated 0.540 configuration, whose 0.5 stripper boil-up preserves saleable C3 purity and whose 40-stage T column is slightly cheaper.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the demonstrated best 0.540 plant (R899) now, then use at most the remaining solves for a low-risk final improvement only if clearly justified.
Boil-up 0.1 over-strips ethane into TTTB, dropping C3 purity to 91% and losing the blend sale; 0.5 is optimal among tested values. R899 combines stripper boil-up 0.5 with a 40-stage T column, saving $0.6M/yr and giving reward 0.540 with $65.9M/yr C3 revenue. Root boil-up 5.5 was harmful and larger stage cuts save little, so preserve all R899 settings. Copying it secures the best valid design before considering any final change.
